except the topbar's review pill is the standard shell, already measured
against its own family boards, so this recipe measures the topbar (which
this board draws as its own instance, 682:4651) and holds the pill.
The probe mounts the real chrome-ui Topbar with the props StudioHeader
builds for the approved state — including the 'Approved by <name> · <ago>'

shell, because reaching an approved round live needs a dashboard that has

WHAT MOVED, and it moved in chrome-ui because THREE boards agree — 681:26
(the topbar board shell-default measures) and both S5 frames, which are
instances of the same component:
· The site name was 13px at the bar's inherited leading. 680:11 is 14/20
on all three, so the site's own name had been rendering at the same size
as the controls around it.
NOT MOVED, and named so the next agent does not re-open it:
· `btn/exit` — the boards say 12px horizontal padding, a 13/18 label and
--flowbite/gray/700; the code ships 10 / 12 / --bk-ink, with a comment
dated 2026-08-03 citing 681:26 for '10 horizontal padding, 12px REGULAR,
ink at gray-900'. The 2026-09-07 capture of that same node says
otherwise, so either the board moved or the earlier read did. Flagged
rather than flipped: the same comment records a deliberate colour

undo, and the exit button belongs to the topbar board's own recipe.
· Everything else on this 1440 frame — rail, drawer, Layers tree, canvas,

THE REVIEW PILL IS ANCHORED AND SKIPPED — the one thing on this board that
is uniquely its own, and the one thing a conformance pass may not settle.
The two boards in this pair paint it two different ways for two states that
both mean 'nothing is blocking you':
130:798 approved  --color/success-tint #DEF7EC ground, success-text
#057A55 label
130:201 pending   --color/warning-tint #FDFDEA ground, ink-soft label
681:26  topbar    warning-tint again, for 'In review · 3 open'
Live, both are gray-100 / ink-soft. That is not drift, it is a written rule:
Topbar.tsx's REVIEW_TONE_CLASS says 'neutral-unless-blocking — info and
success are visually identical by design; only warning gets its own look',
because the bar's colour budget belongs to the two signals that GATE a
publish (the Issues chip and save trouble), and D7 rule 6 caps the bar at two
ambers at once. Painting 'In review' amber spends the third.
So: three boards, two of them mine, disagree with a chrome-ui primitive that
the twelve Shell-state boards already hold at authority=code:topbar. One
screen board does not move that, and neither do two that contradict each
other. Numbers are in measured/<surface>.json; the call is the founder's.
The pill's DOT (680:16 / 680:14) is not anchored either: Figma exports an
ellipse as an with no style props, so the spec carries nothing to
compare, and a 6px status dot whose only content is its colour is the same
design-codex-#6 question the notification rows just answered the other way.
